# Execution directive for build (tag m4), regenerated on 2026-10-22 as the current truth after the owner's direction and the anchor diagnostics (addendum 20: build authorised) (revised, addendum 20)

**Current state: build 27 is authorised (an in-place edit of `run_m4.py` and `onbox_m4.sh`) and launch 11 is pre-authorised once, on the conditions of GATE_COMMIT.md Addendum 20 T12.** This is the measure run m4 of card seed:idea:1: one rented single-GPU box in us-east-1 with the filesystem `metis-env-us-east-1` attached, a

Binding order: this note first, `frozen/ONBOX_CONTRACT.md` (v2) second (item 23 says where this note wins), `out/design_record.json` third; where silent the design record binds as written, GUESS values
included. The build does not read GATE_COMMIT.md. Three standing changes of record: (i) the Python environment is an
artifact built once on the Lambda filesystem and recorded by its lock hash; the on-box script activates it and verifies the hash, and installs
nothing; pins live in the environment record, not in the runner; (ii) implementer selftests are not required and not credited, and the box does not run tests: a separate author writes the tests against the stage interface (section \"Stage interface\") with fixtures recorded on the box, hidden from the builder, and they run locally in a copy of the environment of record before every launch; (iii) a stage failure on the box holds the box open (HOLD) once for a bounded fixer whose every change is committed to git on the box;
the fixer may touch environment and glue, never the measurement protocol or the record fields. The cap is USD 20 of box time (standing rule 1); spend of record USD 6.68; the environment build counts.

## Where to write

The run directory is `/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure`. The build writes exactly `run_m4.py` and
`onbox_m4.sh` there, by absolute path, as in-place edits of the files now present (build 26), and writes nothing anywhere else. It reads the design record
at `/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure/out/design_record.json`, the conventions in `frozen/`
(provenance.py is the record writer; lambda_run.sh and remote_run.sh show what the box does; `ONBOX_CONTRACT.md` is the binding execution
contract) and this note. It does not read `tests/`, `out/`, `results_env/` or `.keys`. `lambda_run_m4.sh` and `remote_run_m4.sh` are the
operator's files. It uses no network. Its only local checks are `python3 -m py_compile run_m4.py` and `bash -n onbox_m4.sh`.

## Checklist of gate changes the build must carry (34 entries) (revised, addendum 20)

**REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH**

1. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Order on the box (revised, addendum 20).** Activate the environment and verify its lock (item 3); capability check
   (item 4); downloads and parameter extraction (item 9); controls (60 s sleep, empty run, unit-and-scale record); anchor
   (serial, then parallel, then the diagnostics of item 19); per-pair docking and analysis (aux timing); AlphaFold timings (seed-major); MD timings; storage; endpoints. There is no tests stage on the box. After an anchor FAIL every later stage still runs (item 11). A
   guard before every stage and unit (item 26). (GATE_COMMIT answers 7, 14, Q5, Q8; Addendum 20 T1, T2.)
2. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Files and payload (rule 5) (revised, addendum 20).** The build writes exactly `run_m4.py` and `onbox_m4.sh` in
   `/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-01/20261021-0509-measure` (absolute path) and reads the design record and `frozen/` only.
   Payload shipped to the box: `run_m4.py onbox_m4.sh remote_run_m4.sh frozen/provenance.py` and `data/` recursively if it exists, all under `~/m4_run/`; no test file is shipped; the environment is the attached filesystem, not payload. Results under
   `~/m4_run/results_m4/out/`, which the launcher fetches. Nothing else is on the box.
3. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Environment of record.** `onbox_m4.sh` sets `VENV=\"${ENV_DIR:-/lambda/nfs/metis-env-us-east-1/m4}/venv\"`,
   exits 2 if it is not an activatable CPython 3.10 venv, activates it and puts `${VENV}/bin` first on PATH before any stage. It computes the lock
   hash as sha256 of the stdout bytes of `\"${VENV}/bin/python\" -m pip freeze` (no flags) and compares it with `ENV_LOCK_SHA256` (forwarded by the launcher, 64 hex
   characters, no default; unset or malformed is exit 2). Mismatch is exit 2 with a void record. The check is one provenance.py record
   `env_check_tag-m4.json` (values: `expected_lock_sha256`, `observed_lock_sha256`, `venv_path`, `python_version`, `equal`). The runner pins nothing and
   reads no `pins.txt`. After a fixer restart (item 6) the lock is recomputed and the records carry the label \"environment changed by the fixer on
   the box; lock <hash>\" when it differs, except that a second mismatch at this very check is final.
4. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Capability check; no installs.** The script and the runner run no `pip`, `apt-get` or `sudo` and
   build no venv. After the lock check, one capability check inside the setup ceiling (item 8), reporting every problem in one pass: import of the
   AlphaFold-Multimer stack and JAX with a GPU device listed; `colabfold_batch --help`; the docking code's entry point `--help` and its
   conformation-generating script's `--help`; OpenMM imported with `Platform.getPlatformByName(\"CUDA\")` succeeding; each tool resolved by
   `shutil.which` against the venv PATH with its absolute path recorded. Any problem is exit 2 with a void record before any GPU stage (item 7), and
   is eligible for the hold (item 6). No trial docking.
5. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Stage interface; no tests on the box (new, addendum 20; replaces the tests stage).** `run_m4.py` implements the section \"Stage interface\" below: one stage per invocation (`--stage <name> --in <dir> --out <dir>`), every external program replaceable through its environment variable, every parser a module-level function by the name given there taking a path and returning a dict (`ValueError` on malformed input; `ParseError` is a subclass of `ValueError`), no work at import (no file, network, subprocess or environment access at module level; `main()` only under `if __name__ == \"__main__\"`). The full run (`--run`) calls the same stage functions in item 1's order. Neither script runs, imports or ships the author's tests; the tests stage, `tests_tag-m4.json` and every reference to `tests/tests_m4.py` in `onbox_m4.sh` and `run_m4.py` are removed. The author's tests run locally before every launch (GATE_COMMIT Addendum 20 T12).
6. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Hold-open and restart: one mechanical check on one file (revised, addendum 20).** The whole requirement is in `onbox_m4.sh`; `run_m4.py` carries no requirement under this item. File: `onbox_m4.sh`. Look for five behaviours in the code that handles an exit-2 stage failure of
   item 7's table. Pass condition: all five are present when the file is read; a review that finds all five reports item 6 satisfied, and a finding on item 6 outside H1 to H5 is advisory. (H1) After a failure other than the 60 s sleep check, once the failed attempt's void records and `RUN_DONE` exist, the
   shell writes `results_m4/out/HOLD` (stage, kind, exit code, UTC time, `hold_seconds`), `hold_seconds` being `HOLD_SECONDS` (forwarded; value of record 2400) capped at 2,400; with `HOLD_SECONDS` unset or 0 no `HOLD` is written and there is no hold. Hold time counts in elapsed time and never in a
   stage ceiling. (H2) It waits for `results_m4/out/RESUME` as item 29 says. (H3) On `RESUME` it computes the sha256 of `run_m4.py` and compares it with the value it took at its own start; any difference is exit 2, label `fixer_out_of_scope`, no restart. (H4) With the hash equal and at least
   1,500 s of REMOTE_TIMEOUT left it moves `results_m4/out` to `results_m4/held_attempt_1/` and runs the runner once from its first stage (item 1's order, every stage, never a mid-run state) under the same T0 and caps, and a `RESUME` never ends the launch in place of that restart; with less than 1,500 s
   left, or on expiry, the launch ends with the first attempt's records. (H5) One hold per launch: an eligible failure in the restarted attempt is exit 2, final, with no second hold. The fixer's scope (environment and glue only; each change committed to git on the box and fetched as `results_m4/out/changes.log`) is
   the operator's procedure; the hash comparison of H3 is its only mechanical test. The labels and summary fields of the hold are item 34.
7. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Broken infrastructure and the exit table (rule 4) (revised, addendum 20).** Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.8, driver 570, python 3.10 and torch 2.7 are preinstalled;
   everything else is in the environment of record. Every outcome maps to exactly one row, and the table is the only source of exit code, `run_valid` and
   the `RUN_DONE` per-input status. Precedence when several rows apply: 2, then 4, then 3, then 0.

   | Event | Exit | run_valid | per-input status |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | environment missing or lock mismatch, capability check problem, download failure, setup total over its ceiling, tool start failure, real tool failure (non-zero exit, crash, missing output), no parsable ranked pose, unparsable rank table, frame guard rejection (item 18), sleep check failed, shell abort before the runner starts | 2 | false | `void_by_failure:<kind>` for every input not decided before it |
   | anchor compared and tolerance missed (the run continues; this row decides the exit at the end, when no row 2 applies) | 4 | false, voided by the anchor, in every record written after the anchor decision | `decided` or `void_by_rule:<reason>` or `unmeasured_by_stop:<kind>` for each of C1 to C4, each with its `calibration_valid` |
   | guard refusal, stage ceiling, tool-call timeout, outer timeout (124, or 137 at the deadline) left at least one input unmeasured, anchor not missed | 3 | as it was | `unmeasured_by_stop:<kind>` for those inputs, `decided` or `void_by_rule:<reason>` for the others |
   | anchor passed and every input decided, or void by rule with no stop (not an A100, zero spread, marginal) | 0 | true | `decided` or `void_by_rule:<reason>` |

   There is no `void_by_anchor_miss` status. Never patch around and never substitute a tool or source: after a failing tool call no second tool or source is tried (a fixer's change under item 6 is not
   the build's patching). Each failure row writes a void record, the summary and `RUN_DONE` before exit. The shell sets its exit trap before the venv step.
   Only the `|| RC=$?` form runs `run_m4.py`, its `--finalize` form and the outer `timeout` under `set -e`; the trap acts only while `FINISHED=0`.
8. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Caps, time and ceilings (rules 1, 2) (revised, addendum 20).** `onbox_m4.sh` reads `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR`, `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` and
   `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` from its environment, with no default above `BUDGET_LEFT_USD=5` or `REMOTE_TIMEOUT=7200`, and stops cleanly, writing a void record for
   unfinished work, before projected spend reaches `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` or elapsed time reaches `REMOTE_TIMEOUT`. Hard cap USD 20 for the run;
   `BUDGET_LEFT_USD` per launch is the lesser of 5 and what remains; every launch uses `REMOTE_TIMEOUT=7200` exactly. It records the `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` seen in
   `env.txt` and `m4_summary.json` (unset: 7200 and the label \"REMOTE_TIMEOUT not forwarded; default 7200 used\"). T0 is the start of the parent
   `remote_run_m4.sh` (`ps -o etimes= -p $PPID`) plus 30 s; unreadable takes 300 s and the label \"bootstrap time assumed 300 s\". Ceilings in seconds:
   setup (items 3, 4 and 9 work, a running total) 1,500; controls and anchor (with its diagnostics) 1,000; per-pair docking and analysis 600 (at most 250 per pair);
   AlphaFold 2,000; MD 1,600 (at most 600 per complex); endpoints 100; margin 400; sum 1,500 + 1,000 + 600 + 2,000 + 1,600 + 100 + 400 = 7,200.
   `allowance(stage) = max(0, min(ceiling(stage), REMOTE_TIMEOUT - elapsed_since_T0 - 400 - 100))`; a stage whose allowance is below its first unit's estimate
   (item 26) is not started. Setup over 1,500 or any call over its limit is exit 2. Spend: `estimated_spend_usd` = seconds since T0 x `PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR` / 3,600
   (pre-T0 seconds reported beside it, not added).
9. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Downloads, nothing interactive, command (rule 10) (revised, addendum 20).** No prompts anywhere. No `sudo`. Downloads only from
   the sources the design names: the PDB entry 6IHB from RCSB and the AlphaFold parameter archive from the AlphaFold project's own storage address; URL and
   sha256 recorded for each; no pip or apt download exists. The archive's sha256 is verified and recorded, it is extracted into `<data>/params` (the `--data`
   directory colabfold is given), the completion marker(s) are the names read from the installed colabfold's own download module (none hard-coded; \"no marker
   named\" recorded if none), and the multimer parameter files for the 5 models are verified present: missing is exit 2. The downloaded `6IHB.pdb` is also copied, byte for byte, to `results_m4/out/6IHB_tag-m4.pdb` (the launcher fetches only that directory; a local diagnostician needs the file itself). No network access in any timed call;
   a timed call whose log shows a download or extraction gets `download_in_timed_call: true`, is not counted and C1 is VOID \"download inside timed call\". A failed
   download stops the run (item 7) with no second source. The `onbox_command` the build returns is one line: `bash remote_run_m4.sh bash onbox_m4.sh`.
10. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Secrets (rule 8).** Nothing reads `.keys`; nothing prints its environment (no `env`, `printenv` or `set` dump; `env.txt` lists only
    named non-secret variables); `HF_TOKEN` is used by downloads only: `onbox_m4.sh` unsets `HF_TOKEN` and `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` after the downloads and
    every tool child gets a copied environment with both removed.
11. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Scope, the calibration branch and the gate scope (rule 3; answer 1) (revised, addendum 20).** Measure the inputs on the card's own protocol; no production phase, no 54-run pilot, no
    216-run grid; anchor first. The anchor's verdict is decided by the anchor alone and never changes (owner ruling 2026-10-22). On an anchor FAIL: the anchor record is FAIL with `run_valid` false; the run is marked invalid before the anchor record is written, so `RUN_VALID.json`, the summary and every later record agree; every later record carries `run_valid` false and `run_valid_voided_by` (the anchor's text) and the label \"measured after an anchor miss; run_valid false, voided by the anchor; calibration_valid decided by this record's own checks only\"; all stages after the anchor still run and C1 to C4 are measured. Every record after the anchor (C1 to C4, the aux, AlphaFold, MD and storage rows summaries) carries `calibration_valid` (true or false) with `calibration_checks` (each check of item 12, its value and its result), decided by those checks only, never by the anchor; `calibration_valid` false makes the record's `decision` VOID with the raw value kept in `measured` and the failed check named as the reason; `calibration_valid` true leaves the decision to the band (item 20 keeps its VOID-by-rule cases). The card's gate (`af2_h_per_run <= 1`) is
    applied to C1 only: C1 values carry `gate_value` 1, `gate_pass` and the card's fallback text in `gate_else` (\"take the docking-plus-MD fallback line with one
    AlphaFold-Multimer seed per pair, or move the grid to 12 pairs\"); C2 and C3 carry `gate: \"not applicable: the card's gate is on af2_h_per_run\"`. The C1 decision
    is the band alone; the run does not branch on the gate. `gate_pass` is computed only when C1 holds a valid measurement (PASS, FAIL or marginal VOID); for any other
    VOID it is null with `gate: \"not evaluated: C1 VOID (<reason>)\"`.
12. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Workload checks and `calibration_valid` per input (new, addendum 20).** `calibration_valid` of a record is the conjunction of its checks; a check that cannot be evaluated is false with a `null_reasons` entry. Common to C1 to C4: the stages before it were not cut by a guard, ceiling or timeout for this input's minimum count (a stop makes the record `unmeasured_by_stop`, `calibration_valid` false, label \"incomplete run: unmeasured inputs are VOID, not holding\"); the 60 s sleep control passed; the GPU was visible. **C1:** per counted run, the pair's FASTA length is in 750 to 1,000 residues; the call's recorded command line has 5 models, 20 recycles, early stopping off and single-sequence input; colabfold exit 0; 5 model structure files and 5 score files exist, are non-empty and parse (at least one ATOM line per structure; each score file loads as JSON); per-model times parsed (or null with a reason, not a failure); no download or extraction in the log; across the input at least 3 counted runs covering all 3 pairs. **C2:** per complex, the built system has 120,000 to 180,000 atoms; both roles present and a nonzero capsid heavy-atom count; the reporter file's last step reaches the equilibration plus 250,000 production steps (0.5 ns at 2 fs) and its energies are all finite (no NaN or inf); the DCD exists with 50 frames (plus or minus one at 5,000 steps per frame); platform CUDA and precision mixed; across the input at least 2 complexes. **C3:** per pair, the docking parameters (swarms, glowworms, steps, setup flags) equal the anchor's; the rank table parses with at least one data row and its top pose file exists and parses with both roles; the interface analysis wrote contacts at 4.5 A, interface residues, distance to the nearest threefold axis and site class, and the call-table row was written as a JSON line; the pair did not reach its 250 s limit; across the input at least 2 pairs. **C4:** each artifact type was measured from files on disk after the runs, nonzero bytes each (AlphaFold outputs of a run that counts in C1, the docking tree of a pair that counts in C3, the MD trajectory and logs of a complex that counts in C2); at least one of each type; `md_setup_bytes` excluded from the value. The anchor record's own `calibration_valid` is true when both poses were obtained and compared (it does not affect its decision).
13. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Pairs, seeds, AlphaFold (answers 2, 3).** 3 stand-in pairs built from chains of the 6IHB entry, one per capsid slot, each a hetero-multimer of
    750 to 1,000 residues (more than one copy of a capsid chain allowed to reach the range); assert each length in range, the three sequences pairwise different,
    the lengths pairwise at least 20 residues apart, one capsid-role and one receptor-role chain set per pair; a failure is exit 2 naming the assertion, no clamp.
    Evidence `results_m4/out/pairs_tag-m4.json` (chain ids and roles, sequences, lengths, sha256 of each FASTA and PDB) and the three FASTA copies, cited in each C
    record's `inputs`. AlphaFold: one GPU; seeds 0, 1, 2 seed-major; 5 models; exactly 20 recycles, early stopping off; single-sequence input only, no sequence database, no
    remote alignment service. Measured = mean wall-clock hours of the whole prediction call per run, first-model compile included (the decision value); rows also carry the
    compile-excluded figure when the log gives per-model times. Minimums: C1 at least 3 completed runs covering all 3 pairs; C2 at least 2 complexes (n recorded); C3 at least 2
    pairs; C4 at least one run of each artifact type; below a minimum the record is VOID and the raw rows stay.
14. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Docking and auxiliary hours (answers 4, 5).** One pip-installed docking code from the environment (name and version read from installed
    metadata, never a constant), same swarm count and parameters for the anchor and every pair, not restrained toward the 6IHB interface, recorded in the anchor record
    (`values.docking_parameters`, `values.docking_order`); the parameters of record (2 swarms, 20 glowworms, 20 steps, seed 0) are not changed; order simulate, conformation generation, `lgd_rank.py` unless `frozen/ONBOX_CONTRACT.md` states another, then that
    order. The top pose is the first row of the tool's own rank list by its score, read under item 28; a missing named pose file or an unparsable rank table is exit 2 with the raw table kept;
    never `sorted(glob)[0]`. aux_h_per_pair = wall-clock hours per pair of docking, interface analysis (contacts at 4.5 A, interface residues, distance to the nearest
    threefold axis, site class) and writing the call-table row; setup, downloads excluded; mean over the finished pairs; a pair reaching 250 s keeps a row
    with `truncated: true`, is not counted, and the loop continues with the next pair; C3 decided if at least 2 pairs finished, else VOID. The frame guard of item 18 applies to each pair's pose.
15. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. MD protocol (answers 5, 10).** One docked complex per pair: the pair's capsid-role chains merged with the top-ranked docking pose of the receptor, one
    structure, chain roles preserved (assert both roles present and a nonzero capsid heavy-atom count before solvation, else exit 2); explicit solvent with water padding
    chosen so the built system has 120,000 to 180,000 atoms (one rebuild inside the complex's 600 s; else C2 VOID with the atom count kept, the range never widened);
    minimise, short equilibration, then a 0.5 ns production segment; one velocity seed (0). The worker writes a DCD trajectory with `DCDReporter` every 5,000 steps
    (`frame_interval_ps` 10 recorded) and a StateDataReporter file, copied to `results_m4/out/` and parsed for the engine ns/day (a file with no rate line gives
    `engine_ns_per_day: null` and the label \"engine rate line missing\"). The decision value is the median over complexes of production steps x timestep over the production
    wall-clock; if it and the engine rate differ by more than 5 percent every ns/day carries \"engine rate and wall-clock disagree\" and both are reported.
16. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Storage (answer 4).** n_storage_gib = apparent bytes written for one grid run (AlphaFold outputs of one run; the whole per-pair docking output tree with
    setup files, swarm directories, rank tables and every pose; the MD trajectory plus every log of the segment: reporter file, stdout and stderr logs, the worker's JSON
    files), intermediates kept, x 216, / 2^30, the decision value. `system.xml`, `solvated.pdb` and checkpoints are `md_setup_bytes`, not in the value. The record also
    carries the 432-run figure, the intermediates-deleted figure and MD bytes per ns (MD bytes over 0.5) as information.
17. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Controls first (answer 7).** After items 3, 4 and 9: the planted 60 s sleep through the same timer (error at most 5 percent, else `run_valid` false, exit 2,
    nothing else runs); the empty-input run, which times the harness itself (the same timer, work-directory creation and record path as a real call, around a no-op command, no
    AlphaFold, JAX, TensorFlow or docking import) and measures the bytes in the directory it created (under 2 s and under 1 MiB, else the excess, only that harness overhead, is
    subtracted from later values and labelled \"setup overhead subtracted\"); one unit-and-scale record, written before any band comparison, `values.kind` \"worked_examples\", whose
    `values.raw_values_in` names the rows files holding the raw AlphaFold seconds, the MD engine rate lines beside the wall-clock ns/day, and the raw bytes per artifact.
18. **REQUIRED FOR LAUNCH. Anchor and its frame guard (answer 8) (revised, addendum 20).** Contact overlap = fraction of 6IHB interface residue-residue contacts (heavy-atom pair at most 4.5 A) the pose also makes, keyed by chain
    role through one chain-mapping function for reference and pose (the receptor chain id \"A\", \"B\" or \"C\" in the file gives the same overlap). Interface backbone RMSD is over N, CA, C, O
    of the receptor residues forming the reference interface (any heavy atom within 4.5 A of the capsid in 6IHB), in the capsid frame, no superposition (the frame is the published capsid's: the pose is moved into it by a translation estimated from the matched capsid atoms; the receptor's orientation is never fitted); the serial-versus-parallel
    top-pose RMSD is over the whole receptor chain and labelled so. **Frame guard (new, addendum 20; a code fix justified by the anchor diagnostics):** after `pose_frame_shift`, the capsid residual RMSD over the matched atoms is computed; if it exceeds 0.1 A, or fewer than 99 percent of the pose's capsid heavy atoms match (by chain, residue number, insertion code and atom name), or none match, the pose is not scored and the stage raises exit 2, kind `anchor_frame`, keeping the raw pose and the numbers in `anchor_frame_diagnostic_tag-m4.txt`; never an anchor miss, and the centre-of-atoms fallback and the \"leave the pose where it is\" branch of `pose_frame_shift` are removed. The frame shift, matched count and residual are recorded in the anchor record (`values.frame`) and in the pairs' rows. No Kabsch fit. ## Stage interface

`python3 run_m4.py --stage <name> --in <dir> --out <dir>` runs exactly one stage on the inputs in `--in` (an earlier stage's outputs under their full-run file names, or a fixture recorded on the box) and writes only under `--out`; exit codes 0, 2, 3 and 4 as item 7 (the `anchor` stage returns 4 on a miss; the full run `--run` continues past it and exits by precedence at the end). The time and budget variables of item 8 (and `M4_T0_EPOCH`, `M4_PRE_T0_SECONDS`, `M4_VENV`, `M4_VENV_BIN`) are read from the environment as in a run, so a test can set a different `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` and check that the guard arithmetic follows it. Importing `run_m4.py` does no work.

- **Stage names:** `capability` (items 3's record, 4), `downloads` (item 9), `controls` (item 17), `anchor` (items 18 and 19; serial, parallel, diagnostics), `aux` (item 14), `af2` (item 13), `md` (item 15), `storage` (item 16), `endpoints` (items 11, 12, 20, 21; reads the rows and decides every input). A stage that needs an earlier stage's output reads it from `--in` and exits 2 naming the missing file if it is absent; it never runs the earlier stage itself.
- **External programs, one environment variable each (default: the real program by absolute venv path; the variable holds a path or command word, so a test can put a replay program in its place):** `M4_COLABFOLD` (`colabfold_batch`), `M4_LIGHTDOCK_SETUP` (`lightdock3_setup.py`), `M4_LIGHTDOCK` (`lightdock3.py`), `M4_LGD_GENERATE` (`lgd_generate_conformations.py`), `M4_LGD_RANK` (`lgd_rank.py`), `M4_MD_WORKER` (the OpenMM worker command), `M4_NVIDIA_SMI` (`nvidia-smi`), `M4_FETCH` (the download command), `M4_SLEEP` (the planted-sleep command), `M4_PYTHON` (the interpreter used for capability probes).
- **Parsers (module-level; each takes a path and returns a dict; `ValueError` on malformed input; the stage turns it into a failed record and exit 2, never a default):** `parse_nvidia_smi_header`, `parse_nvidia_smi_query`, `parse_etimes`, `parse_colabfold_log`, `parse_reporter_file`, `parse_engine_rate_line`, `parse_rank_table` (item 28; the dict carries rows, columns, mapping and the top row), `parse_af2_timing_rows` (path to a rows JSON-lines file), `parse_pdb` (atoms by chain, residue number, insertion code and atom name).
- **Pure functions callable by name (take values, return values):** `contact_overlap`, `interface_backbone_rmsd`, `whole_chain_rmsd`, `rmsd_no_superposition`, `pose_frame_shift`, `score_pose_against_native`, `independent_anchor_score`, `anchor_decision`, `decide_band`, `is_marginal`, `gate_on_c1`, `spread_check`, `relative_sd`, `storage_from_bytes`, `ns_per_day_from_wallclock`, `rates_disagree`, `cost_usd`, `stop_at_seconds`, `stage_allowance_s`, `calibration_checks_c1`, `calibration_checks_c2`, `calibration_checks_c3`, `calibration_checks_c4` (item 12; each returns the checks with values and results, and the conjunction).

2881: def water_padding_nm(atoms: list, target_atoms: int = 150000) -> float:

2884:     xs = [a["x"] for a in atoms]

4211: def threefold_axis_distance(points: list) -> float:
4212:     if not points:

4214:     n = float(len(points))
4215:     centre = (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n,

4781:

4799:                           "path": str(docking_dirs[0]), "bytes": b, "kind": "docking",
4800:                           "counts_in": True, "intermediate": True,
4801:                           "source": str(docking_dirs[0])})
4802:     md_dirs = [p.get("md_work") or find_dir(f"md_{p['pair']}") for p in pairs]
4803:     md_dirs = [Path(d) for d in md_dirs if d]
4804:     md_bytes = 0
4805:     md_setup_bytes = 0

4917: def decide_exit_code(state: RunState) -> int:
4918:     """The exit table's precedence: 2, then 4, then 3, then 0.
4919: 
4920:     Row 3 applies only when a guard, a ceiling or a timeout actually stopped
4921:     work and left an input unmeasured. An input a stage simply does not measure
4922:     is not a stop.
4923:     """
4924:     if state.failure_kind or (not state.run_valid and not state.anchor_missed):
4925:         return EXIT_INFRA
4926:     if state.anchor_missed:
4927:         return EXIT_ANCHOR
4928:     if state.unmeasured_inputs() and state.stop_events:
4929:         return EXIT_GUARD
4930:     return EXIT_OK

4933: def measure_from_rows(state: RunState, cid: str, rows: list):
4934:     """One input's decision value, from the raw rows alone."""
4935:     if cid == "C1":
4936:         summary = parse_af2_timing_rows_text(rows)
4937:         return summary["mean_h"], summary["n"]
4938:     if cid == "C2":
4939:         rates = []
4940:         for r in rows:
4941:             if r.get("incomplete") or not r.get("atoms"):
4942:                 continue
4943:             rate = r.get("wallclock_ns_per_day")
4944:             if rate is None and r.get("production_wallclock_s"):
4945:                 rate = ns_per_day_from_wallclock(
4946:                     r.get("steps") or MD_PRODUCTION_STEPS,
4947:                     r.get("timestep_fs") or MD_TIMESTEP_FS,
4948:                     r.get("production_wallclock_s"))
4949:             if rate is not None:
4950:                 rates.append(rate)
4951:         return (statistics.median(rates) if rates else None), len(rates)
4952:     if cid == "C3":
4953:         hours = []
4954:         for r in rows:
4955:             if r.get("truncated") or r.get("incomplete") or r.get("seconds") is None:
4956:                 continue
4957:             hours.append(r.get("hours")
4958:                          if r.get("hours") is not None
4959:                          else r.get("seconds") / 3600.0)
4960:         return ((sum(hours) / len(hours)) if hours else None), len(hours)
4961:     if cid == "C4":
4962:         counted = [r for r in rows
4963:                    if r.get("counts_in") is not False and r.get("bytes") is not None]
4964:         total = sum(int(r.get("bytes") or 0) for r in counted)
4965:         if not counted:
4966:             return None, 0
4967:         scaled = storage_from_bytes(max(0, total - state.overhead_bytes))
4968:         return scaled["gib_216_runs"], len(counted)
4969:     return None, 0

4972: def stage_endpoints(state: RunState) -> dict:
4973:     """Close the run: every input gets a record, then the summary is written."""
4974:     started = state.clock()
4975:     anchor_name = f"endpoint-anchor_tag-{TAG}.json"
4976:     present = any(state.input_path(f"rows_{arm}_tag-{TAG}.jsonl") is not None
4977:                   for arm in ("af2", "md", "aux", "storage")) \
4978:         or state.input_path(f"pairs_tag-{TAG}.json") is not None \
4979:         or state.input_path(anchor_name) is not None
4980:     if not present and not state.failure_kind and not state.stop_events:
4981:         raise HarnessFailure(
4982:             f"the stage needs rows_af2_tag-{TAG}.jsonl and it is not in the inputs",
4983:             f"looked in {state.indir} and {state.outdir}", kind="missing_input")
4984:     ensure_anchor_record(
4985:         state, why=(f"{LABEL_ANCHOR_NOT_REACHED}: "
4986:                     + (state.run_valid_voided_by or state.failure_kind
4987:                        or "; ".join(e["reason"] for e in state.stop_events)
4988:                        or "the run ended before the anchor stage")))
4989:     for cid in INPUT_IDS:
4990:         name = f"endpoint-{cid}_tag-{TAG}.json"
4991:         if name in state.records_written or (state.outdir / name).exists() \
4992:                 or state.input_path(name) is not None:
4993:             continue
4994:         rows_arm = {"C1": "af2", "C2": "md", "C3": "aux", "C4": "storage"}[cid]
4995:         rows = load_rows(state, rows_arm)
4996:         measured, n = measure_from_rows(state, cid, rows)
4997:         if state.failure_kind:
4998:             why = ("the run ended on broken infrastructure: "
4999:                    f"{state.run_valid_voided_by or state.failure_kind}")
5000:         elif state.stopped and measured is None:
5001:             stop_names = "; ".join(e["reason"] for e in state.stop_events)
5002:             why = f"{LABEL_UNMEASURED} ({stop_names})"
5003:         else:
5004:             why = None
5005:         emit_input_record(
5006:             state, cid, measured, n=n, rows_arm=rows_arm,
5007:             start_epoch=started, end_epoch=state.clock(),
5008:             void_reason=why, rows=rows, stop_kind=state.last_stop_kind())
5009:     state.exit_code = decide_exit_code(state)
5010:     write_env_note(state)
5011:     write_summary(state)
5012:     write_run_valid(state)
5013:     state.stages_done.append("endpoints")
5014:     return {"records": list(state.records_written), "exit_code": state.exit_code}

240:     rec.setdefault("values", {})["calibration_valid"] = False
241:     rec["values"].setdefault("calibration_checks", [
242:         {"check": "run_completed", "result": False, "value": False,
243:          "null_reason": reason}])
244:     rec["notes_list"] = [INCOMPLETE]
245:     rec["tag"] = "m4"
246:     with open(path, "w") as fh:
247:         json.dump(rec, fh, indent=2)
248:         fh.write("\n")
249: 
250: put(os.path.join(out, "endpoint-anchor_tag-m4.json"),
251:     {"stage": "anchor", "endpoint": "anchor", "tag": "m4"},
252:     "the anchor redocking was not compared: the run ended before it finished",
253:     {"measured": None, "published": ("AAVR-PKD2 bound to the AAV2 spike region "
254:                                      "adjacent to the icosahedral three-fold axis "
255:                                      "(PDB 6IHB)"),
256:      "tolerance": {"min_contact_overlap": 0.5,
257:                    "max_interface_backbone_rmsd_a": 5.0,
258:                    "max_serial_parallel_rmsd_a": 2.0},
259:      "unit": "fraction of published contacts, and angstrom",
260:      "null_reasons": {"measured": reason}},
261:     {"min_contact_overlap": 0.5, "max_interface_backbone_rmsd_a": 5.0},
262:     "an anchor the run never compared is VOID, never holding",
263:     reason)
264: 
265: # An input the measuring program already decided keeps that decision. Its
266: # record is read, never rewritten, and it is not shown as void below. Only an
267: # input with no such record takes this script's status. Code 4 (the anchor
268: # missed) voids all four, whatever their records say.
269: UNMEASURED = "unmeasured, not holding"
270: 
271: def standing(cid):
272:     """Read one input's record on disk: decided, void by a rule, or not done."""
273:     path = os.path.join(out, "endpoint-%s_tag-m4.json" % cid)
274:     try:
275:         rec = json.load(open(path))
276:     except Exception:
277:         return None
278:     if not isinstance(rec, dict):
279:         return None
280:     decision = rec.get("decision")
281:     values = rec.get("values") or {}
282:     why = str(values.get("void_reason") or values.get("voided_by") or "")
283:     notes = " ".join(str(n) for n in (rec.get("notes_list") or []))
284:     if decision in ("PASS", "FAIL"):
285:         return {"status": "decided", "decision": decision, "voided_by": None}
286:     if decision == "VOID" and UNMEASURED not in why and UNMEASURED not in notes:
287:         if values.get("marginal") or why:
288:             return {"status": "void_by_rule:%s" % (why or "marginal"),
289:                     "decision": "VOID", "voided_by": why or "marginal"}
290:     return None
291: 
292: KEPT = {} if code == 4 else {c: s for c in CARD for s in [standing(c)] if s}
293: 
294: for cid, (key, unit, value, band) in CARD.items():
295:     if cid in KEPT:
296:         continue
297:     put(os.path.join(out, "endpoint-%s_tag-m4.json" % cid),
298:         {"stage": "endpoints", "input": cid, "key": key, "tag": "m4"},
299:         "%s was not measured: the run ended before this stage" % key,
300:         {"measured": None, "unit": unit, "card_value": value, "band": band,
301:          "n": 0, "void_reason": "unmeasured, not holding (%s)" % reason,
302:          "null_reasons": {"measured": reason}},
303:         {"band": band, "card_value": value},
304:         "an input the run never reached is VOID, never holding",
305:         reason)
306: 
307: inputs = {}
308: for c in ("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"):
309:     if c in KEPT:
310:         inputs[c] = dict(KEPT[c])
311:     else:
312:         inputs[c] = {"status": status, "decision": "VOID", "voided_by": reason}
313: 
314: summary = {}
315: summary["what_this_run_decides"] = WHAT
316: summary["tag"] = "m4"
317: summary["written_by"] = "onbox_m4.sh, because the measuring program left no marker"
318: summary["run_valid"] = run_valid
319: summary["run_valid_voided_by"] = reason
320: summary["exit_code"] = code
321: summary["inputs_status"] = inputs
322: summary["remote_timeout_seen_s"] = os.environ.get("M4_VOID_TIMEOUT")
323: summary["notes"] = [INCOMPLETE]
324: sp = os.path.join(out, "m4_summary.json")
325: if not os.path.exists(sp):
326:     with open(sp, "w") as fh:
327:         json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
328:         fh.write("\n")
329: 
330: with open(valid_path, "w") as fh:
331:     json.dump({"run_valid": run_valid, "voided_by": reason, "stopped": code == 3,
332:                "inputs_status": inputs, "tag": "m4"}, fh, indent=2)
333:     fh.write("\n")
334: 
335: with open(os.path.join(out, "RUN_DONE"), "w") as fh:
336:     json.dump({"exit_code": code, "run_valid": run_valid, "voided_by": reason,
337:                "stopped_by": [reason], "inputs": inputs, "tag": "m4",
338:                "finished_utc": now,
339:                "notes": [INCOMPLETE]}, fh, indent=2)
340:     fh.write("\n")
341: print("[onbox] minimal void written: code %d run_valid %s" % (code, run_valid))
342: PY
343: }

345: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
346: # 3. The marker, armed before anything can fail.
347: #
348: # The trap is set here, before the environment is built, so that an abort in
349: # the install still leaves a record, a validity file and a marker behind. A run
350: # that dies silently is indistinguishable from a run that was never started,
351: # and that has cost real money before. The trap acts only while FINISHED is 0;
352: # every route below sets FINISHED=1 before its own exit.
353: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
354: 
355: FINISHED=0
356: SETUP_USED=0
357: HELD_ATTEMPTS=0
358: ENV_CHANGED_BY_FIXER=false
359: LOCK_OBSERVED=""
360: HOLD_LABELS=""
361: HOLD_SIGNAL=""
362: # The environment of record, on the filesystem the launcher attached. It is not
363: # built here and nothing is installed into it.
364: VENV="$ENV_DIR/venv"
365: 
366: # The measuring program, hashed now, before anything can change it. A repair
367: # made while the box is held open may change the environment and the glue
368: # around it; it may not change this file, and this hash is how that is checked
369: # before the run is restarted.
370: sha_of() { [ -f "$1" ] && sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1 || echo "missing"; }
371: RUNNER_SHA_AT_START="$(sha_of "$RUNNER_PY")"

373: # The compute table, written on every exit whatever decided the run. Every
374: # stage of the run's order is listed, whether it ran or not; a stage that was
375: # running when the run ended is closed with the time it had.
376: write_compute_summary() {
377:   M4_CS_OUT="$OUT" M4_CS_PRICE="$PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR" \
378:   M4_CS_INSTANCE="${INSTANCE_TYPE:-}" M4_CS_T0="$T0_EPOCH" \
379:   python3 - <<'PYC' >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || say "the compute table could not be written"
380: import json, os, time
381: 
382: out = os.environ["M4_CS_OUT"]
383: os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
384: now = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
385: now_epoch = time.time()
386: try:
387:     t0 = float(os.environ.get("M4_CS_T0") or now_epoch)
388: except ValueError:
389:     t0 = now_epoch
390: elapsed = max(0.0, now_epoch - t0)
391: price = float(os.environ.get("M4_CS_PRICE") or 0) or None
392: 
393: STAGES = ["capability", "downloads", "controls", "anchor",
394:           "aux", "af2", "md", "storage", "endpoints"]
395: path = os.path.join(out, "compute_table_tag-m4.json")
396: table = None
397: if os.path.exists(path):
398:     try:
399:         table = json.load(open(path))
400:     except Exception:
401:         table = None
402: if not isinstance(table, dict):
403:     table = {}
404: 
405: by_name = {}
406: for entry in table.get("stages", []):
407:     if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("stage"):
408:         by_name[entry["stage"]] = entry
409: 
410: rows = []
411: for name in STAGES:
412:     entry = by_name.get(name) or {}
413:     row = {
414:         "stage": name,
415:         "ran": bool(entry.get("ran")),
416:         "reason": entry.get("reason") or ("not started" if not entry.get("ran") else None),
417:         "start_utc": entry.get("start_utc"),
418:         "end_utc": entry.get("end_utc"),
419:         "wall_clock_s": entry.get("wall_clock_s"),
420:         "gpu_busy_s": entry.get("gpu_busy_s"),
421:         "gpu_busy_reason": entry.get("gpu_busy_reason") or "not sampled",
422:         "gpu_name": entry.get("gpu_name"),
423:         "exit_code": entry.get("exit_code"),
424:     }
425:     if row["ran"] and row["end_utc"] is None:
426:         row["end_utc"] = now
427:         if row["start_utc"]:
428:             try:
429:                 start_epoch = time.mktime(
430:                     time.strptime(row["start_utc"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
431:                 row["wall_clock_s"] = round(now_epoch - start_epoch, 3)
432:             except Exception:
433:                 row["wall_clock_s"] = None
434:         row["reason"] = row.get("reason") or "cut short when the run ended"
435:     rows.append(row)
436: 
437: table = {
438:     "stages": rows,
439:     "instance_type": os.environ.get("M4_CS_INSTANCE") or None,
440:     "price_usd_per_hour": price,
441:     "elapsed_since_t0_s": round(elapsed, 3),
442:     "estimated_spend_usd": round((elapsed / 3600.0 * price) if price else 0.0, 4),
443:     "anchor_decision": table.get("anchor_decision"),
444: }
445: with open(path, "w") as fh:
446:     json.dump(table, fh, indent=2)
447:     fh.write("\n")
448: 
449: summary_path = os.path.join(out, "m4_summary.json")
450: summary = {}
451: if os.path.exists(summary_path):
452:     try:
453:         summary = json.load(open(summary_path))
454:     except Exception:
455:         summary = {}
456: if not isinstance(summary, dict):
457:     summary = {}
458: summary.setdefault("what_this_run_decides",
459:                    "This run decides the stand-in protocol only.")
460: summary["compute"] = table
461: if "run_valid" not in summary:
462:     summary["run_valid"] = None
463:     summary["run_valid_voided_by"] = "the measuring program wrote no summary"
464: with open(summary_path, "w") as fh:
465:     json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
466:     fh.write("\n")
467: print("[onbox] compute table written")
468: PYC
469: }

471: on_exit() {
472:   local code=$?
473:   write_compute_summary
474:   if [ "$FINISHED" = "0" ]; then
475:     say "aborted before the measuring program finished (shell code $code)"
476:     if [ ! -f "$OUT/RUN_DONE" ]; then
477:       write_minimal_void 2 "the on-box script aborted before the measuring program finished" \
478:         "void_by_failure:shell_abort"
479:     fi
480:     write_compute_summary
481:     exit 2
482:   fi
483:   exit "$code"
484: }
485: trap on_exit EXIT

487: finish() {
488:   local code="$1"
489:   write_env_txt
490:   write_compute_summary
491:   say "finished with exit code $code"
492:   FINISHED=1
493:   exit "$code"

523: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
524: # 6. The python environment of record.
525: #
526: # The environment was built once on the filesystem the launcher attached, and
527: # it is named by its lock: the hash of the list of packages inside it. This
528: # script turns it on, asks it for that list, and refuses to measure anything
529: # unless the hash matches the one the launcher forwarded. Nothing is installed
530: # here, nothing is upgraded, and no package is pinned by this script: the pins
531: # live in the environment, which is why the lock is the thing that is checked.
532: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
533: 
534: VENV_PY=""
535: 
536: note_hold_label() {
537:   HOLD_LABELS="${HOLD_LABELS:+$HOLD_LABELS|}$1"
538: }

540: # write_env_check <observed> <equal: true|false> <python version> <why>
541: #   One record of the environment check, through the shared record writer, with
542: #   the same keys every other record carries.
543: write_env_check() {
544:   M4_EC_OUT="$OUT" M4_EC_FROZEN="$RUN_DIR/frozen" M4_EC_VENV="$VENV" \
545:   M4_EC_EXPECTED="$ENV_LOCK_SHA256" M4_EC_OBSERVED="$1" M4_EC_EQUAL="$2" \
546:   M4_EC_PYVER="$3" M4_EC_WHY="$4" M4_EC_PRICE="$PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR" \
547:   M4_EC_INSTANCE="${INSTANCE_TYPE:-}" M4_EC_HELD="$HELD_ATTEMPTS" \
548:   M4_EC_FIXER="$ENV_CHANGED_BY_FIXER" \
549:   python3 - <<'PY' >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || say "the environment-check record could not be written"
550: import json, os, sys, time
551: 
552: out = os.environ["M4_EC_OUT"]
553: os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
554: now = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
555: equal = os.environ["M4_EC_EQUAL"] == "true"
556: expected = os.environ["M4_EC_EXPECTED"] or None
557: observed = os.environ["M4_EC_OBSERVED"] or None
558: fixer = os.environ["M4_EC_FIXER"] == "true"
559: held = int(os.environ["M4_EC_HELD"] or 0)
560: 
561: # Every key the records of this run carry about the machine. One that this
562: # script cannot read on its own says so, in words, beside the value.
563: unread = "not read by onbox_m4.sh; the measuring program reads it from the box"
564: machine = {
565:     "instance_type": os.environ["M4_EC_INSTANCE"] or None,
566:     "gpu_name": None, "gpu_driver": None, "cuda_runtime_version": None,
567:     "cuda_plugin_version": None,
568:     "start_utc": now, "end_utc": now,
569:     "price_usd_per_hour": float(os.environ["M4_EC_PRICE"] or 0) or None,
570:     "expected_lock_sha256": expected,
571:     "observed_lock_sha256": observed,
572:     "venv_path": os.environ["M4_EC_VENV"],
573:     "environment_changed_by_fixer": fixer,
574:     "held_attempts": held,
575: }
576: reasons = {k: unread for k, v in machine.items() if v is None}
577: values = {
578:     "kind": "environment_check",
579:     "expected_lock_sha256": expected,
580:     "observed_lock_sha256": observed,
581:     "venv_path": os.environ["M4_EC_VENV"],
582:     "python_version": os.environ["M4_EC_PYVER"] or None,
583:     "equal": equal,
584:     "machine": machine,
585:     "null_reasons": reasons,
586: }
587: 
588: sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["M4_EC_FROZEN"])
589: try:
590:     import provenance
591: except Exception:
592:     provenance = None
593: 
594: path = os.path.join(out, "env_check_tag-m4.json")
595: rec = None
596: if provenance is not None:
597:     try:
598:         provenance.write_result(
599:             path + ".tmp",
600:             cell={"stage": "environment check", "tag": "m4"},
601:             inputs=[{"path": os.environ["M4_EC_VENV"], "sha256_full": observed,
602:                      "what": "the environment of record, by its lock sha256"}],
603:             metric="the sha256 of the package list of the environment of record",
604:             values=values,
605:             threshold={"expected_lock_sha256": expected},
606:             decision_rule=("the environment is the one of record only when the "
607:                            "hash of its package list equals the lock the "
608:                            "launcher forwarded; anything else stops the run"),
609:             decision="PASS" if equal else "FAIL",
610:             notes=os.environ["M4_EC_WHY"])
611:         rec = json.load(open(path + ".tmp"))
612:         os.remove(path + ".tmp")
613:     except Exception:
614:         rec = None
615: if rec is None:
616:     rec = {"cell": {"stage": "environment check", "tag": "m4"}, "inputs": [],
617:            "metric": "the sha256 of the package list of the environment of record",
618:            "values": values, "threshold": {"expected_lock_sha256": expected},
619:            "decision_rule": "the hash of the package list must equal the lock",
620:            "decision": "PASS" if equal else "FAIL",
621:            "notes": os.environ["M4_EC_WHY"],
622:            "env": {"timestamp_utc": now, "host": None, "python": None,
623:                    "git_rev": None}}
624: rec["kind"] = "env_check"
625: rec["run_valid"] = equal
626: rec["run_valid_voided_by"] = None if equal else os.environ["M4_EC_WHY"]
627: rec["notes_list"] = ([] if not fixer else
628:                      ["environment changed by the fixer on the box; lock %s"
629:                       % (observed or "unknown")])
630: rec["tag"] = "m4"
631: with open(path, "w") as fh:
632:     json.dump(rec, fh, indent=2)
633:     fh.write("\n")
634: print("[onbox] environment check written: equal %s" % equal)
635: PY
636: }
637: 
638: # The two steps of this section. Each sets ATTEMPT_RC and ATTEMPT_KIND and
639: # returns non-zero instead of exiting, so the hold below can decide what
640: # happens next.
641: LOCK_MISMATCH_SEEN=0
642: 
643: activate_environment() {
644:   local setup_start pyver
645:   setup_start="$(date -u +%s)"
646:   VENV_PY="$VENV/bin/python"
647:   [ -x "$VENV_PY" ] || VENV_PY="$VENV/bin/python3"
648:   if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ] || [ ! -f "$VENV/bin/activate" ]; then
649:     say "FATAL: $VENV is not a python environment that can be turned on"
650:     write_minimal_void 2 "the environment of record is missing or cannot be activated" \
651:       "void_by_failure:environment_missing"
652:     ATTEMPT_RC=2
653:     ATTEMPT_KIND="environment_missing"
654:     ATTEMPT_STAGE="the environment of record"
655:     return 1
656:   fi
657:   pyver="$("$VENV_PY" -c 'import platform,sys;print(platform.python_implementation()+" "+"%d.%d.%d" % sys.version_info[:3])' 2>>"$LOG")"
658:   case "$pyver" in
659:     "CPython 3.10."*) : ;;
660:     *)
661:       say "FATAL: the environment of record is not a CPython 3.10 one (got '${pyver:-nothing}')"
662:       write_minimal_void 2 "the environment of record is not an activatable CPython 3.10 environment" \
663:         "void_by_failure:environment_missing"
664:       ATTEMPT_RC=2
665:       ATTEMPT_KIND="environment_missing"
666:       ATTEMPT_STAGE="the environment of record"
667:       return 1 ;;
668:   esac
669:   ENV_PYTHON_VERSION="$pyver"
670:   # shellcheck disable=SC1091
671:   . "$VENV/bin/activate"
672:   export VIRTUAL_ENV="$VENV"
673:   export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH"
674:   export M4_VENV="$VENV"
675:   export M4_VENV_BIN="$VENV/bin"
676:   RUNNER_CMD=("$VENV_PY" "$RUNNER_PY")
677:   say "the environment of record is on: $pyver at $VENV"
678:   SETUP_USED=$(( SETUP_USED + $(date -u +%s) - setup_start ))
679:   return 0
680: }
681: 
682: verify_lock() {
683:   local setup_start observed freeze_rc expected
684:   setup_start="$(date -u +%s)"
685:   expected="$(printf '%s' "$ENV_LOCK_SHA256" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
686:   if ! printf '%s' "$expected" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'; then
687:     say "FATAL: no readable environment lock was forwarded (ENV_LOCK_SHA256)"
688:     write_env_check "" "false" "${ENV_PYTHON_VERSION:-}" \
689:       "ENV_LOCK_SHA256 was unset or not 64 hexadecimal characters"
690:     write_minimal_void 2 "the environment lock was not forwarded, so the environment could not be checked" \
691:       "void_by_failure:env_lock"
692:     ATTEMPT_RC=2
693:     ATTEMPT_KIND="env_lock"
694:     ATTEMPT_STAGE="the environment lock check"
695:     LOCK_MISMATCH_SEEN=1
696:     return 1
697:   fi
698:   # The list is written out first and hashed from the file, so the hash is of
699:   # exactly the bytes the environment printed, and the list itself is kept.
700:   freeze_rc=0
701:   "$VENV_PY" -m pip freeze > "$OUT/env_pip_freeze.txt" 2>>"$LOG" || freeze_rc=$?
702:   observed="$(sha_of "$OUT/env_pip_freeze.txt")"
703:   [ "$observed" = "missing" ] && observed=""
704:   SETUP_USED=$(( SETUP_USED + $(date -u +%s) - setup_start ))
705:   LOCK_OBSERVED="$observed"
706:   if [ "$freeze_rc" != "0" ] || [ -z "$observed" ]; then
707:     say "FATAL: the environment of record would not list its own packages"
708:     write_env_check "$observed" "false" "${ENV_PYTHON_VERSION:-}" \
709:       "the environment would not list its packages (exit $freeze_rc)"
710:     write_minimal_void 2 "the environment of record would not list its own packages" \
711:       "void_by_failure:env_lock"
712:     ATTEMPT_RC=2
713:     ATTEMPT_KIND="env_lock"
714:     ATTEMPT_STAGE="the environment lock check"
715:     LOCK_MISMATCH_SEEN=1
716:     return 1
717:   fi
718:   if [ "$observed" = "$expected" ]; then
719:     say "the environment lock matches: $observed"
720:     write_env_check "$observed" "true" "${ENV_PYTHON_VERSION:-}" \
721:       "the package list of the environment hashes to the lock the launcher forwarded"
722:     return 0
723:   fi
724:   # A lock that differs after a repair is the repair, and it is labelled as
725:   # such. A lock that differs twice at this very check is final.
726:   if [ "$HELD_ATTEMPTS" -ge 1 ] && [ "$LOCK_MISMATCH_SEEN" = "0" ]; then
727:     ENV_CHANGED_BY_FIXER=true
728:     note_hold_label "environment changed by the fixer on the box; lock $observed"
729:     say "the environment was changed by the fixer on the box; lock $observed"
730:     write_env_check "$observed" "false" "${ENV_PYTHON_VERSION:-}" \
731:       "environment changed by the fixer on the box; lock $observed"
732:     return 0
733:   fi
734:   say "FATAL: the environment lock does not match (observed $observed)"

function.name: bash
function.description:
Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.

Be aware: OS: linux, Shell: bash

All commands run in the current working directory by default. Use the `workdir` parameter if you need to run a command in a different directory. AVOID using `cd <directory> && <command>` patterns - use `workdir` instead.

Use `/tmp/opencode` for temporary work outside the workspace. This directory has already been created, already exists, and is pre-approved for external directory access.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location
   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use `ls foo` to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., rm "path with spaces/file.txt")
   - Examples of proper quoting:
     - mkdir "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)
     - mkdir /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail)
     - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct)
     - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail)
   - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command.
   - Capture the output of the command.

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds. If not specified, commands will time out after 120000ms.
  - If the output exceeds 2000 lines or 51200 bytes, it will be truncated and the full output will be written to a file. You can use Read with offset/limit to read specific sections or Grep to search the full content. Do NOT use `head`, `tail`, or other truncation commands to limit output; the full output will already be captured to a file for more precise searching.

  - Avoid using Bash with the `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or when these commands are truly necessary for the task. Instead, always prefer using the dedicated tools for these commands:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT find or ls)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT grep or rg)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
    - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple bash tool calls in a single message. For example, if you need to run "git status" and "git diff", send a single message with two bash tool calls in parallel.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single Bash call with '&&' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before Bash for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.
    - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)
  - AVOID using `cd <directory> && <command>`. Use the `workdir` parameter to change directories instead.
    <good-example>
    Use workdir="/foo/bar" with command: pytest tests
    </good-example>
    <bad-example>
    cd /foo/bar && pytest tests
    </bad-example>

# Git and GitHub
- Only commit, amend, push, or create PRs when explicitly requested.
- Before committing, inspect `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log --oneline -10`; stage only intended files and never commit secrets.
- Write a concise commit message that matches the repo style.
- Do not update git config, skip hooks, use interactive `-i`, force-push, or create empty commits unless explicitly requested.
- If a commit fails or hooks reject it, fix the issue and create a new commit; do not amend the failed commit.
- Before creating a PR, inspect status, diff, remote tracking, recent commits, and the diff from the base branch.
- Review all commits included in the PR, not just the latest commit.
- Use `gh` for GitHub tasks, including PRs, issues, checks, and releases; return the PR URL when done.

workdir.description: The working directory to run the command in. Defaults to the current directory. Use this instead of 'cd' commands.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files. 

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file. 
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + colon + space (e.g., `1: `). Everything after that space is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the oldString or newString.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `oldString` is not found in the file with an error "oldString not found in content".
- The edit will FAIL if `oldString` is found multiple times in the file with an error "Found multiple matches for oldString. Provide more surrounding lines in oldString to identify the correct match." Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replaceAll` to change every instance of `oldString`. 
- Use `replaceAll` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

newString.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Replace all occurrences of oldString (default false)

function.name: glob
function.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches as a batch that are potentially useful.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

function.name: grep
function.description:
- Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size
- Searches file contents using regular expressions
- Supports full regex syntax (eg. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+", etc.)
- Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (eg. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")
- Returns file paths and line numbers with matching lines
- Use this tool when you need to find files containing specific patterns
- If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`.
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: File pattern to include in the search (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file or directory from the local filesystem. If the path does not exist, an error is returned.

Usage:
- The filePath parameter should be an absolute path.
- By default, this tool returns up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- The offset parameter is the line number to start from (1-indexed).
- To read later sections, call this tool again with a larger offset.
- Use the grep tool to find specific content in large files or files with long lines.
- If you are unsure of the correct file path, use the glob tool to look up filenames by glob pattern.
- Contents are returned with each line prefixed by its line number as `<line>: <content>`. For example, if a file has contents "foo\n", you will receive "1: foo\n". For directories, entries are returned one per line (without line numbers) with a trailing `/` for subdirectories.
- Any line longer than 2000 characters is truncated.
- Call this tool in parallel when you know there are multiple files you want to read.
- Avoid tiny repeated slices (30 line chunks). If you need more context, read a larger window.
- This tool can read image files and PDFs and return them as file attachments.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file or directory to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines to read (defaults to 2000)

function.name: write
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.
